TEXT.English: [BOLD]Day 34[\BOLD][NEWLINE]We came across some old Patrian ruins that looked promising. Keefri did one of those quick detection spells she's apt to do and warned us of some undead lurking inside.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][ITALICS]"Well, where there's undead, there's treasure, right?"[\ITALICS] I said. Jenkin laughed. She didn't. Oh well.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]It ended up being two floors of what I can only assume was once an alchemy lab. There were a couple of skellies (what alchemist raises skeletons anyways?) and an overgrown rat (I guess it befriended the skellies), but that's about it.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]A few rusted alchemy tools and a bag of coins was the hoard they were guarding. A bit disappointing.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Jenkin spotted a hatch that led to a second floor. Keefri did her thing again and detected nothing, so we hopped down.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]By all appearances, it looked like someone beat us to the loot. There were a couple of large chests already open and emptied and the floor was littered with the scattered bones of what I'm pretty sure were more skelly guards (armored this time).[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Very disappointing.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]I'm not sure who out there likes to explore underground lairs from the bottom-up, but whoever they are forgot to close up the giant tunnel they dug. Jenkin wanted to explore the thing despite us being low on torches. Keefri did not. I had to side with Keefri on this one.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]I'll see about organizing a proper expedition later to find out where that tunnel leads and see who dug it.[NEWLINE]-Journal entry of an Austrin explorer

TEXT.English: "Any good dwarf knows the underground isn't empty. Often, you'll mine straight into a cave that hasn't seen light since Kilmorph laid the stone you're standing on. Occasionally, you'll find something strange.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]We've found a couple of tunnels not mined by us. Now, we haven't run into whoever made them yet, but that may be for the best... One of the boys found tools in one of those tunnels, and what I can tell you is that they were not crafted by dwarven hands."[NEWLINE]- account from a Khazad miner during the Age of Ice

The addition of chaos [magic/spells] to the [ritual/magic/spell] makes them very [malleable/susceptible] for my [mages/adepts] to mold like clay. I have ordered the [beasts/slaves] to dig deeper while my [mages/adepts] continue their work. I will update you if further [modification/creation] is required."[NEWLINE]- partially translated message recovered from an ancient Patrian quarry

TEXT.English: "Let me tell you, Captain, these molefolk offered us some of the most beautiful gems I ever laid eyes on. I know you say I exaggerate a lot, but it's the truth! You should have seen the way they gleamed under my torch! I almost wept at the sight of them.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Better yet, I think they have a whole hoard of the treasure waiting to be traded. While they led me through their home, I spied with my little eye a whole caravan of them carrying even bigger gems into some side-cave.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]I ask my molefolk friend if I could take a look. You know, all diplomatically.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]They said no![NEWLINE][NEWLINE]I asked why. All diplomatically.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]They said it was none of my business![NEWLINE][NEWLINE]I'm telling you, Captain, that sounds like a treasure hoard to me!"[NEWLINE]- letter sent from a Lanun trader

TEXT.English: "-Okay, so this lad, Votrur, has this uncanny ability to predict where a vein of ore will be, down to the centimeter. If he says we'll find iron twenty meters to the south, we mine twenty meters to the south![NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The only time he's been wrong - and I use "wrong" loosely" - is that time he said we'd find mithril 40 meters to the west of the Rulvir Branch. We knew that crossed over to mole territory, but it was mithril, so we didn't care too much about hurting the bramblenoses' feelings.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]About 20 meters in we break into a mole mine! And it wasn't one of those cutesy little tunnels they like to dig, it was MASSIVE! I mean, I've been to the mines in the mountainhomes, and I swear that place could measure up to some of them![NEWLINE][NEWLINE]And you know what Votrur said? He said we should try digging down west for 20 more meters! Can you believe it! As if we weren't in the middle of a giant mole mine![NEWLINE][NEWLINE]I don't think Votrur has ever tried to predict a mithril vein since then! Though you could-[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Huh? Oh, yeah, the moles saw us! I think it caused some sort of incident up above with the overseers, but that's not important. What IS important is my punchline, which is that you could say Votrur-"

We knew that crossed over to mole territory, but it was mithril, so we didn't care too much about hurting the bramblenoses' feelings.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]About 20 meters in we break into a mole mine! And it wasn't one of those cutesy little tunnels they like to dig, it was MASSIVE! I mean, I've been to the mines in the mountainhomes, and I swear that place could measure up to some of them![NEWLINE][NEWLINE]And you know what Votrur said? He said we should try digging down west for 20 more meters! Can you believe it! As if we weren't in the middle of a giant mole mine![NEWLINE][NEWLINE]I don't think Votrur has ever tried to predict a mithril vein since then! Though you could-[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Huh? Oh, yeah, the moles saw us! I think it caused some sort of incident up above with the overseers, but that's not important. What IS important is my punchline, which is that you could say Votrur-"

TEXT.English: "We smelled it far before we reached it. When we arrived at its entrance, the smell was so pungent that some of my men broke ranks to puke and gasp for air. I can't even describe the smell other than it was awful enough to make me wonder if the molemen had begun dabbling in something worse than necromancy.[NEWLINE]The burrow itself was just another hole in the ground, though much larger than what we saw in the city. I waited for our cleric to finish puking before ordering some light, then steeled myself to march in.[NEWLINE]That's when we all heard a terrible roar come from inside."[NEWLINE]-Bannor commander

TEXT.English: Of the beastmen that populate Erebus, the molemen were late arrivals, having been created by a circle of mages during the latter days of the Patrian Empire. Using a specialized combination of life and body rituals, their creators imbibed the molemen's bodies with the ability to physically morph into specialized niches through the repeated use of spells and constant repetition of tasks. While serving their Patrian masters, the molemen quickly proved to be excellent miners, excavators, and masons.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The fall of the Patrian Empire came before the molemen could spread across Erebus. Warfare and chaos struck down their masters, forcing them to flee into the mines and quarries they had dug. There they would hide, waiting out the rest of the civil war under the flames of social collapse.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Soon after the Age of Ice began. The longer winters and endless snows would force many on the surface to seek shelter underground. Borderline-feral by this time, the molemen proved no match for the more organized arrivals and would be pushed further underground, into caves and tunnels.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]This cycle of downwards migration, encroachment, and fleeing continued as the Age of Ice worsened for those on the surface, until the molemen fled so deep into the underdark that none dared to pursue.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]In this darkness is where what would become known as Kusekh society formed. Packs and bands became proper tribes. Settlements formed and their numbers grew. New mines were dug, disparate caverns were connected by intricate tunnel networks, and, for a time, it seemed as if the underdark would prove to be a stable home.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]It wouldn't be until near the end of the Age of Ice that the Kusekh stumbled upon the shadow dragons. It started as a series of disappearances on the periphery, with scouts failing to return to their villages. Then the search parties disappeared. Then entire villages. Panic spread as rumors of an encroachment by a great dragon took root within Kusekh society.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Either out of hubris or desperation, the leaders of the Kusekh assembled an army to face this new threat. Only a handful of warriors returned, telling a horror story of not one, but dozens of shadow dragons so large they filled caverns and tunnels and so eager to gorge upon molemen that they twisted and climbed over each other to reach them.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]And so again they fled, this time upwards, hunted and pursued as they climbed higher and higher.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]With Mulcarn dead and the ice thawing, the first molemen breach the surface for the first time since the Age of Magic.

TEXT.English: The the Kusekh are sluggish on the surface, but make up for it through their unique infrastructure and line of promotions. [H1]Infrastructure[\H1] [NEWLINE][BOLD]Roads[\BOLD]: The Kusekh build a network of tunnels instead of roads. While slightly more expensive to build, they can only be used by molekin units, meaning enemy units will always traverse your tiles as if there were no roads built. [NEWLINE][BOLD]Surface Tunnels[\BOLD]: The Kusekh trade the gradual evolution of Forts for Surface Tunnels, which act both as mines and relay points for your city units to immediately transport to. Any molekin unit that enters a tile with a Surface Tunnel gains the Tunnel Access promotion, which allows them to teleport for short distances. TEXT.English: Mesyx is a reluctant leader, one who would have preferred giving the burden to someone else rather than himself. Yet unlike many, he remembers the surface and the Patrians who made the first molekin.[NEWLINE]He remembers the metal armor they wore, crafted by the minerals he mined.[NEWLINE]He remembers the walls of stone they erected, stone that he himself had to claw from the ground.[NEWLINE]He remembers their faces and how different they were from his.[NEWLINE]He remembers their cruelty.[NEWLINE]And these memories of the surface world and their civilizations have brought him wisdom.[NEWLINE]While others squabbled and made fiefdoms out of caverns, he united tribes.[NEWLINE]While others attacked outsiders or fled, he made peace.[NEWLINE]While others dug deeper, he was cautious.[NEWLINE]And now the others are dead, and he remains.

TEXT.English: When their Patrian masters fell, they fled deep into their mines. When the dwarves dug into their mines, they fled deeper into caverns and tunnels.. When the lizardfolk, the humans, the beasts, and so many more sought shelter from the endless cold in their caves, they fled yet again, into the darkness of the underdark.[NEWLINE]All they seemed to do was flee. All it ever did was make Skrylyx more embittered.[NEWLINE]Eventually they fled too deep and came across monsters that had gestated in the darkness for centuries.[NEWLINE]His kin fled again. Skrylyx did not.[NEWLINE]Where they saw terror, Skrylyx saw power. He wanted this power, by any means necessary.[NEWLINE]And somewhere in the darkness, something answered his desires.

TEXT.English: It is said that during the Age of Ice, lone molemen would transition into a feral state to survive. Over the years this changed their bodies into a more beastly form.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Whether this is true or not is up for debate. What is known is that wherever the Kusekh dig, these creatures are often working alongside them.

TEXT.English: By the Age of Rebirth, the Kusekh have partially learned to direct the process that allows their bodies to change. Deep burrows are made to serve as incubators for what will become burrowers. Whatever the process is that they've developed, it involves large quantities of food, namely livestock. These burrows are placed far outside of Kusekh cities, and many outsiders have mistaken them for monster lairs due to their pungent smell and piles of refuse at their entrances.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]While they may appear to be giant animals, burrowers display incredible intelligence and, on occasion, have been seen to speak. They act as the backbone of Kusekh society, quickly digging out intricate tunnel systems during times of peace, and acting as giant troop transports during times of war.

TEXT.English: Years of careful feeding and continuous work further shape the burrower's bodies. Elder burrowers are called Excavators, and they live up to their namesake. Solid granite seems to churn and melt as these underground titans work, and it only takes a matter of hours for one to do what an entire mining crew would need months for.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]It is said that a group of excavators can hollow out an artificial cavern so large it has its own weather system.

TEXT.English: When the Kusekh go to war, a pungent smell of rot and death begins to permeate the deep burrows that usually gestate burrowers. Within days, gorgers begin to claw their way out.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]A ravenous monster, their appetite can never be sated for long. They charge headlong into enemy lines, grabbing terrified soldiers and biting down on their flesh. Whenever a Kusekh army is on the move, Gorgers may be found wandering nearby, feasting on local farms and livestock.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Mages who have examined gorger corpses have detected traces of body magic, though what rituals the Kusekh use to create them is a closely guarded secret.

TEXT.English: Whereas scouts chart valleys and mountains, the molemen explore caverns and caves. Delvers lead the Kusekh's underground exploration, warning their companions of dangers and unstable ground. Whatever cave a surface-dweller discovers, there is a good chance a delver already knows of it.

TEXT.English: Even now, the underdark holds a strange allure for the Kusekh. Rarely, this allure takes a stranglehold on a moleman, prompting them to delve deeper into the earth where the shadow dragons roam. Sometimes they come back, morphed into a form that is almost unrecognizable to those that knew them.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Dredgers can twist and contort their bodies in ways that even other molemen find uncanny. Some say even their bones are malleable, to the point that they can push themselves through the smallest cracks in the stones.

TEXT.English: "...There is scant evidence on what the molemen were up to during the Age of Ice, but we do know that the dwarves encountered them from time to time. While Luchuirp accounts correctly identified them as beastkin like the lizardfolk, Khazad miners were apparently so spooked by their encounters that it spawned the legend of the Bramblenose, an earth spirit that serves as an ill-omen for for those who wander too deep into caverns.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The Bramblenose legend became so prevalent that overseer of the Grimlock Mines, Dalrok Kazor, offered a reward of 1,000 gold pieces for whoever could prove the existence of the elusive creature..."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]- Darlas Dunmore [ITALICS]"On the Beastkin of Erebus"[\ITALICS]

TEXT.English: Over time a dragon cult has formed around Mondrinth among the Kusekh. Warriors calling themselves "stoneclaws" graft stone and gems onto their bodies, hoping to emulate the scales of the fang dragon. This tradition naturally meshes with their innate ability to transform their bodies, slowly making their skin appear as if it were made of the earth itself.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Stoneclaws are seen as the elites of Kusekh armies. During wars, they will pillage surface settlements and mines, collecting any gems they find for themselves and as tribute to Mondrinth.

TEXT.English: No one can say why Mondrinth took pity on the molemen, not even the dragon himself. Perhaps it was their connection to the earth, which reminded him of his creator. Perhaps he saw in them a way to obtain more beautiful gems. Perhaps it was a disdain for the creations of Esus seeping into a domain that should be Kilmorph's. And perhaps it was a matter of loneliness, brought by the silence of the Compact.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The dragon shook the thought from his head. He moved through the ground like it was water, passing through hills and mountains but somehow never disturbing the earth. He breached in one of the Kuskekh burrow cities, settling down as a crowd watched in awe. Many watched in awe, some bowed in respect or religious fervor, and a few, he noted, backed away nervously.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]A few minutes passed before an entourage, led by the city's chief and head mage, approached. Behind them were a few burrowers laden with gems. A mix of adepts and soldiers unloaded the gems carefully in front of the dragon in two separate piles. Mondrinth could see there was a silent tension between the two groups, and it didn't take a genius to figure out that they saw their tributes as some kind of factional powerplay for his favor.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The mage opened his mouth to speak, only to be interrupted by the chief,[NEWLINE]"Please, great Mondrinth, accept our humble tribute. These are the finest gems we mined this season, handpicked by us just for you."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Such formal respect!
